Bumped near the 400 Metres.  Near the 250 Metres became unbalanced when bumped by WINNING MACHINE which lay out.  J Orman stated that he was given the option of holding a more forward position.  He said when PANDA LEGEND commenced well he elected to go forward but was obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Trainer W Y So confirmed the instructions issued.
Slow to begin.

Y L Chung stated that his instructions were to go forward and lead if possible.  He said as a consequence he rode his mount along in the early stages to comply with those instructions but when unable to cross runners to his inside ISLAND GOLDEN was obliged to race very wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Trainer K L Man confirmed the instructions and stated he issued those instructions as he felt ISLAND GOLDEN would not be able to make up ground in the Home Straight if it settled back in the field.
L Ferraris stated that the horse would be better suited with the reapplication of blinkers.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
In the early stages raced keenly.  When being crossed by YEE CHEONG RAIDER leaving the 1000 Metres got its head up when being restrained to avoid that runner.

Shifted out at the start and was bumped.  Apprentice P N Wong stated that her mount raced wide although it was able to obtain cover.  She added that in the Home Straight GOOD FORTUNE did not respond to her riding and felt "flat”.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Shifted in shortly after the start and was bumped.  Leaving the 1100 Metres raced keenly and was steadied to avoid CALL TO COMMAND.   A Badel stated that his mount did not run out the 1400 Metres of today’s race.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be a "roarer” which had previously been reported.

Shifted in near the 300 Metres and was bumped.  H Bowman reported that his mount did not respond to his riding when placed under pressure in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Near the 1100 Metres was steadied to avoid GENERAL SMART when racing keenly.  RATTAN GALAXY continued to race keenly in the middle stages.  Near the 300 Metres was bumped by BEAUTY MISSILE which shifted in.  As a result RATTAN GALAXY then shifted in and brushed IRON LEGION.

Bumped at the start.  Brushed near the 300 Metres.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Y L Chung stated that he was obliged to race wide and without cover in the early stages.  He said when GENERAL SMART shifted out after the 800 Metres his mount was bumped by GENERAL SMART and taken wider and did not finish the race off thereafter.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

On jumping was crowded between SPEEDY TRIDENT and THE WAY WE WIN.  In the middle stages raced keenly and after the 800 Metres was shifted to the outside of SPEEDY TRIDENT.  Z Purton stated that his intention was to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages.  He said when GENERAL SMART jumped well and the pace of the event was only moderate he was able to hold an on-pace position without having to pressure his mount to do so.  He added that GENERAL SMART was disadvantaged by IRON LEGION being positioned to his outside and as a result gave ground in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

On jumping made contact with GENERAL SMART and then shortly after blundered.  M L Yeung reported that the instructions were to go forward.  Trainer Y S Tsui confirmed the instructions and stated he issued those instructions as the horse had not been finishing its races off in recent starts.

L Ferraris stated that with an expected lack of pace in the event the connections had requested him to go forward.  He said when HAPPY BOSS jumped well and the pace of the event was run outside of standard time in the early stages he was able to comply with those instructions.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Sent for sampling post-race.

Near the 1100 Metres, when racing keenly, was steadied to avoid HAPPY BOSS (L Ferraris) which shifted in when not clear.  L Ferraris was reprimanded and advised to ensure that he is sufficiently clear when shifting ground.

For a short distance near the 350 Metres had difficulty obtaining clear running.  Trainer P C Ng advised that he had instructed K Teetan to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages as the horse had been finishing its races off only fairly when ridden in a forward position.

From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Near the 900 Metres was tightened to the inside of CHEERFUL WONGCHOY.  Approaching the 800 Metres TYCOON EXPRESS was then steadied when crowded by CHEERFUL WONGCHOY which shifted in when it continued to race ungenerously.  Over the final 50 Metres could not be ridden out when racing in restricted room between GOLDEN WIN and LIGHTNESS OF BEING which was giving ground.  J Moreira stated that his mount was reluctant to race inside other horses and after settling back in the field found it difficult to make up ground in the Home Straight, particularly with the early stages of the event being run outside of standard time.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Shortly after the start was steadied when crowded between VICTOR THE RAPID and GORGEOUS VICTORY which shifted out.  SUPREME VOYAGER was then shifted across behind runners in the early stages from a wide barrier.

Apprentice P N Wong stated that after leading the event her mount gave ground in the Home Straight and made a respiratory noise.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be a "roarer” which had previously been reported.

When questioned regarding his riding Z Purton stated that he had expected to settle back in the field from the outside barrier and had been instructed to endeavour to take runs to the inside as connections felt that it had been advantageous to race in this position having regard to the racing pattern today.  He said as a consequence after settling back in the field he elected to remain racing behind GORGEOUS VICTORY and SUPREME VOYAGER rather than shifting out on the Home Turn to start a forward move.  He said after improving to the inside of CHATER FLASH near the 400 Metres he endeavoured to secure clear running between CHATER FLASH and SMILING CHAMPION.  He added that as he commenced to improve between those two runners CHATER FLASH shifted in slightly and SMILING CHAMPION lay out which resulted in the run becoming too tight to improve into and as a consequence JUBILANT STAR was held up for clear running between the 300 Metres and the 150 Metres where he then shifted to the outside of CHATER FLASH to obtain clear running.  Trainer D J Hall confirmed the instructions and stated he issued those instructions as he was of the opinion that it would be advantageous to improve close to the rail.  Noted to have lost its left hind plate after the race.

Lay out in the early stages of the Home Straight.  J Orman confirmed that from an inside barrier he was instructed to make use of that barrier and hold a more forward position than it did at its first race start.

Shortly after the start got its head up, shifted out and made contact with FULL OF LAUGHTER.  Throughout the early and middle stages raced ungenerously and near the 1000 Metres got its head up when being steadied to avoid CONRAD PATCH.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, CHATER FLASH will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
Shortly after the start was checked when crowded between GORGEOUS VICTORY which shifted in slightly and CHATER FLASH which got its head up and shifted out despite the efforts of its rider.
Sent for sampling post-race.

Shifted out on jumping and made contact with LUCKY BID.  L Hewitson (TOP THRONE) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 800 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in when not clear of BABY SAKURA, resulting in BABY SAKURA having to be checked to avoid TOP THRONE.  L Hewitson was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Wednesday, 29 April 2026 at Happy Valley.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his very good race riding record.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Near the 900 Metres, when racing keenly, was steadied to avoid CHARMING LEGEND which shifted in after being taken out.  C L Chau stated that after making a forward move from the 600 Metres his mount made contact with CHARMING LEGEND shortly after and then on the Home Turn became badly unbalanced when it contacted with CHARMING LEGEND.  He added subsequent to that incident GHORGAN finished the race off in a one-paced manner in the Home Straight. C Y Ho (ALL’S WELL) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 1000 Metres he allowed his mount to shift out when insufficiently clear of CHARMING LEGEND, resulting in CHARMING LEGEND losing its rightful running and being checked to avoid ALL’S WELL.  C Y Ho was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Sunday, 19 April 2026 at Sha Tin.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his very good race riding record.  After the 600 Metres CHARMING LEGEND commenced to race keenly which resulted in it having to be steadied to avoid ALL’S WELL near the 500 Metres.  J Moreira reported that as a result CHARMING LEGEND became positioned too close to the heels of ALL’S WELL and struck the heels of ALL’S WELL on a number of occasions thereafter.  Near the 500 Metres was shifted to the outside of ALL’S WELL and made contact with GHORGAN.  A short distance later CHARMING LEGEND became badly unbalanced when buffeted for room between GHORGAN and ALL’S WELL (C Y Ho) which shifted out when being steadied to avoid OUTGATE when positioned too close to that runner’s heels.  As the Stewards were satisfied that Jockey Ho was obliged to shift out to avoid the heels of OUTGATE, no direct action was taken, however, he was advised to exercise more care in similar circumstances.  J Moreira stated that after being checked near the 1000 Metres and badly crowded on the Home Turn CHARMING LEGEND was unable to finish the race off in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Jumped only fairly.  Held up on the Home Turn.  Near the 350 Metres was shifted to the outside of SELF IMPROVEMENT to continue into clear running.  A short distance later SELF IMPROVEMENT shifted out whilst giving ground, resulting in GORGEOUS WIN having to be steadied and shifted to the inside of SELF IMPROVEMENT to obtain clear running.

K Teetan reported that his mount hung out throughout the event and near the 700 Metres was steadied to avoid CRIMSON FLASH.  He added that in the Home Straight PAKISTAN LEGACY did not respond to his riding.  Trainer W Y So stated that he had been pleased with the horse leading into the race.  He said the horse had not previously demonstrated a tendency of hanging out and he attributed this to the fact that it was racing tight to the inside of SELF IMPROVEMENT and CRIMSON FLASH throughout the middle stages.  He added that the horse is better suited when it is able to dictate in the lead.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of PAKISTAN LEGACY was considered disappointing as compared to its previous race starts.  Before being allowed to race again, PAKISTAN LEGACY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

Shifted out at the start and was bumped.  A Atzeni (CRIMSON FLASH) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that between the 1000 Metres the 800 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in, resulting in SELF IMPROVEMENT being unnecessarily crowded for room between that section of the race and then also contributed to SELF IMPROVEMENT having to be restrained when it lost its rightful running between CRIMSON FLASH and PAKISTAN LEGACY which hung out.  A Atzeni was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Wednesday, 29 April 2026 at Happy  Valley.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his excellent race riding record.
